transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
The White House has announced that the U.S. Ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle,
has been asked to resign.
NPR's Franco Ordonez reports the announcement was made this morning by new White House Press
Secretary Katie Zacharia.
President Trump told reporters on Monday that he was not happy with Guilfoyle and that he
was considering firing her.
Zacharia broke the news that Guilfoyle was asked to step down during her first briefing
in front of the White House press corps.
We have asked Ambassador Guilfoyle to resign.
She has been a wonderful asset to the team and we wish her well.
Guilfoyle is a former top Trump campaign aide and former fiancée of Donald Trump Jr., the
president's son.
The Wall Street Journal first reported last week that Guilfoyle had asked a donor to pay
a $100,000 credit card bill.
She allegedly asked him to wire the money to avoid a paper trail.
Franco Ordonez, NPR News, the White House.
We are learning more about why immigration agents searched the home of a sitting Congresswoman.
NPR's Lou Garrett reports that the investigation into Ohio Democratic Representative Ilhan Omar
deals with immigration fraud allegations.
Foreign security investigation agents started searching Omar's DC home early Monday morning.
Her neighbor, 79-year-old Sharon Jackson, says it began at 4.30 a.m.
The DOJ says it's part of a federal criminal investigation.
Current and former federal officials with knowledge of the search, but who weren't authorized
to speak publicly about it, confirmed details of this investigation.
They tell NPR this search is part of a multi-year probe that includes whistleblower complaints
and the investigation centers on immigration fraud allegations.
Omar, a U.S. citizen and former Somalian refugee, has long denied these charges.
She called the search of her DC home political targeting.
Lou Garrett, NPR News, Washington.
A sentencing takes place in Las Vegas today for the man accused of orchestrating the murder
of rap icon Tupac Shakur in 1996.
Steve Futterman is in Las Vegas and prepared this report.
It was six weeks ago that Dwayne Davis, a former gang leader, was found guilty.
We, the jury in the above entitled case, find the defendant Dwayne Keith Davis guilty of
first degree murder with use of a deadly weapon.
Today Davis will find out what his sentence will be.
During the trial, jurors heard testimony describing the 30-year-old drive-by attack of Shakur as
a revenge gang killing.
Prosecutors from the start said they would not seek the death penalty, but Davis could
still be sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole.
Before the sentence is announced, there will be victim impact statements which could include
relatives of Shakur.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Futterman in Las Vegas.
You're listening to NPR News.
President Trump will fly to Alaska today to campaign for incumbent Republican Senator
Dan Sullivan.
Trump has been stumping for GOP candidates, but in states that Republicans usually carry.
After tonight's rally outside Anchorage, Trump will overnight in Las Vegas.
Tomorrow he'll join another campaign rally in Arizona.
Formula One has signed a 10-year deal with Rwanda to host Grand Prix races in the country,
starting in the early 2030s.
The events will mark the first F1 race on African soil in over 30 years, as NPR's Jewel
Bright reports.
Formula One says the races will be called the African Grand Prix, and will be held on the
new purpose-built circuit in Pugsera near Rwanda's capital Kigali.
It will be the first F1 race in Africa since the 1993 South African Grand Prix.
F1 officials say they hope the race will offer an opportunity for the sport to expand its
profile across Africa.
Rwanda's President Paul Kagame has held the deal, saying it will attract skills, tourism
and investment to Rwanda.
However, the event is likely to face opposition from human rights groups, who have accused
Rwanda of using sports to improve its international image amid widespread government crackdowns
on political opposition and press freedom.
Jewel Bright, NPR News, Lagos.
Pope Leo has arrived at a Rome hospital for surgery.
He announced over the weekend he's having a small, localized nodule removed from one
of his lungs.
The Vatican says it expects him to take a week to recover.
It's NPR.

topics.text: White House asks U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign over $100,000 credit card bill
Immigration agents search Rep. Ilhan Omar's Washington home in multi-year immigration fraud probe
Sentencing set today in Las Vegas for Dwayne Davis, convicted of ordering 1996 Tupac Shakur murder
President Trump to campaign in Alaska for Senator Dan Sullivan, then Las Vegas and Arizona
Formula One signs 10-year deal to host African Grand Prix races in Rwanda starting early 2030s
Pope Leo enters Rome hospital for surgery to remove a small lung nodule
